findings.text: the manifest's tests/baseline_suite fields describe the guard gate as 'base arm (the driver exactly as at the base revision 8ccc6ed1)' and 'same test, different driver', but the actual script sets BASE_REV=$(git -C "$W" rev-parse HEAD) at submission time (which the log confirms was 15b3aa2f891f49525cad9df4bad3f9d5a6cda281, itself already carrying this node's full 167-insertion/43-deletion driver rewrite, not the original 8ccc6ed1) and only checks out the TEST FILE at that revision into a scratch copy; both the base and head pytest invocations then run against the SAME live driver (benchmarks/coil_edit_latency.py in the worktree, reached via PYTHONPATH="$W" in both arms). So the gate actually varies the test-file SELECTION (3 tests vs 4 tests) while holding the driver fixed, which is the inverse of what is claimed, and it never runs any test against the driver as it stood at the true base revision 8ccc6ed1 — so it cannot detect a regression the 210-line driver rewrite itself introduced relative to the pre-node code, which is presumably what a driver A/B is for.

git diff --stat 8ccc6ed1..269bcbaa shows benchmarks/coil_edit_latency.py (167 insertions, 43 deletions) and docs/figures/forward-solve-api/coil-edit-nonconvergence/diagnose_branch_terms.py (12 insertions, 16 deletions) were both modified by this node's commits, and both paths sit inside the node's own declared write scope (the first is named verbatim in orientation_write_paths, the second is under the coil-edit-nonconvergence figure directory also named there), but neither appears in the manifest's changed_paths list; per this node's own CONTRACT ('a coordinator cannot see your tree, so an unfilled field reads as no work'), the driver rewrite that everything else in the manifest depends on is the one file missing from the record of what changed.

the checkpoint quotes the coordinator ruling as verbatim ('Ruling text as received') and has it read '...persisting its 8 states beside the constrained archive...', but the actual ruling on disk at resume-4-advice.txt reads '...persisting its 20 states beside the constrained archive...' and also carries an explanatory sentence ('your constrained arm reads 4 of 20 converged, and the S18 session measured 4 of 20 on the H200 at HEAD against the banked 10 of 20 without any constraint') that the quoted text drops entirely while still presenting the surrounding text as a direct quotation; the number actually delivered (20 states per arm) matches the real ruling, so this is a transcription defect in the record rather than an execution defect.

justifications.durability: every log and JSON receipt the manifest cites (two-arm-1275764 table/census/log, guard-gate-1275858.log, guard-control-1275864.log, connectivity-gate-1275907.log, the sbatch scripts) is present on disk under the run directory and I read each one directly; the census and two-arm-table numbers reproduce byte-for-byte what the manifest's evidence_inputs quotes. The record is durable and independently readable, which is why the guard-gate mischaracterization above was catchable at all — the defect is in what the record claims the script measures, not in whether the record persists.
justifications.evidence: the central scientific claim — the unconstrained control arm reproduces the banked fixture exactly (converged/drawn_closed/axis_enclosing_cycle counts and index sets) while the constrained arm diverges, so the census discrepancy is the constraint's own effect — is independently verified against census-control.txt (CENSUS_AGREES=1) and census-constrained.txt, and the evidence doc's 125/0 additive diff is confirmed by git diff --numstat. Against that, the guard-gate's own script proves its 'different driver' framing false (finding 1), and the changed_paths omission (finding 2) means the coordinator's view of 'what changed' is missing the one file every downstream claim rests on.
justifications.fit: no plan/stage/sprint label or version suffix appears in any of the five commits' diffs or filenames, and the figure/test naming follows the existing coil-edit-nonconvergence conventions; the scope-extension to tests/test_flux_surface_connectivity.py is declared explicitly rather than silently absorbed, and is authorised by the coordinator ruling that names the symbol it touches (PERSISTED_STATE_TERMS).
justifications.goal_fidelity: the node's actual mandate under the coordinator's ruling — run one control arm, table it state for state against the constrained arm, re-base expectations only if the control confirms the drop is the constraint's own effect — is fulfilled and the control does confirm it, so the headline deliverable (a re-based, correctly-attributed fixture) is sound. What falls short is the driver-regression half of the done-when: the guard gate that is supposed to show 'zero added failures against base' never actually exercises the driver as it stood at base, so that specific claim is not established by the evidence presented, only assumed from a test that does not test it.
justifications.scope_discipline: the node stayed within its declared write paths — both under-reported files (benchmarks/coil_edit_latency.py, the figure directory's diagnose_branch_terms.py) are inside orientation_write_paths, so this is a completeness defect in changed_paths rather than a boundary violation; git diff on the base checkout is otherwise unremarkable, and the extension to tests/test_flux_surface_connectivity.py is both declared and authorized rather than reached for silently.
